gate_decision.reason: The literal q36/g32 radix-4 PCS proof verifies on SBF; the 10-bit lookup evaluator replays every economic attack; and the LogUp corpus now has seven vectors including the multiplicity-after-chi order attack. But the pre-registered 16-seed variance criterion fails (range 55,786 CU vs 29,056 headroom) and the linear=128 stress row breaches the strict ceiling on its own (+32,024 CU), so candidate_green is withdrawn. Every reading including the combined worst case clears the 1.19M target.
gate_decision.headline: No one-transaction product claim until a real radix-4 proof with the LogUp lookup and fixed-width RLC verifies on SBF below the stated gate. The strict 10%-slack ceiling fails the pre-registered worst-of-16 draw criterion by 26,730 CU and the bracket top by 10,965 CU (k'=83-corrected); closing it requires a further named shrink or a documented gate-rule decision on per-draw variance.

next_measurements: Name a further shrink (>= ~11K CU for the bracket top, ~35K for the worst draw, ~67K combined) or take an explicit documented gate-rule decision on per-draw variance before quoting any strict-slack claim.
Integrate the tested fixed-table LogUp main/helper columns, the multiplicity column, and both sum(h)=0 claims into the C1/C2 statement proof under the v4 envelope (soundness note section 8).
Integrate the gamma-power table and fixed-width outer-lazy dot at the corrected k'=83 width into the real wide PCS parser rather than adding its isolated total arithmetically.
Generate the real statement proof with radix-4 commitments and run the complete SBF transaction five times, including economic and proof-corruption attacks.
caveat: The 678,407-CU radix-4 result is a real q36/g32 two-phase PCS verification with fresh roots, grinding nonce, queries, and proof bytes; the 16-seed study shows it sits within 0.2% of the fixed-shape mean, with a 55,786-CU worst-of-16 range. The fixed-width wide RLC and lookup-range composition remain isolated SBF measurements at the pre-recount k80 width, and the lookup exists as a no-proof semantic oracle. Their sum is a feasibility projection, not an end-to-end payment proof or a closed product gate.
